security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel PDIS sample-record parser checks bit 63 of pdisadr1/pdisadr2 for address validity instead of the new ADR1V/ADR2V fields in pdishdrev, OR consumes the right-shifted physical/guest-physical address from pdisadr2 without left-shifting by 2 bits to recover the full address.
security_spec.summary: PDIS v1.0 record format redefines address-validity from bit[63] self-tagging to explicit ADR1V/ADR2V header bits, and encodes physical addresses right-shifted-by-2 in pdisadr2 (matching PMP/PTE encoding for XLEN-beyond addresses); kernel perf/KVM consumers using the pre-v1.0 interpretation will leak bogus virtual/physical addresses into userspace profiles.

findings.finding: CSR_VSISELECT/CSR_VSIREG are defined for AIA (IMSIC indirect register access), not for PDIS/Sspdis/Smpdis. No PDIS-related CSRs (spdisdata, mpdisctl, pdisadr1/2, pdishdrev, etc.) are defined anywhere in the kernel.
This is IMSIC (AIA) indirect CSR access code using VSISELECT/VSIREG for interrupt controller configuration. It has no relationship to PDIS sample-record parsing.

The Linux kernel does not implement the RISC-V Smpdis/Sspdis (Pointer Discovery and Instruction Sampling) extension. No sample-record parsing code exists. There is no code to check bit 63 of pdisadr1/pdisadr2 for address validity, nor code that consumes right-shifted physical addresses from pdisadr2. The vulnerability condition described in the security spec cannot be triggered because the component is not implemented.
findings.snippet: No PDIS-related code found anywhere in arch/riscv/ or the broader kernel tree. Searched for: pdisadr1, pdisadr2, pdishdrev, spdisdata, mpdisctl, spdisamb, spdisevmask, spdisfilter, pdislat, pdistime, pdisevtype, pdiscnt, Sspdis, Smpdis.
